title: If you think girl workouts are bad NOW, wait till you see the 80s
summary: A comedic roast of a 1988 women's workout tape with Cory Everson, mocking pink dumbbells, partial crunches, light-weight 'toning' and the sexualized camera work. NH argues women's fitness still pushes ineffective toning and diet culture, that women should build muscle through intelligent bulks, and that simply training like men is not the answer either.
claims: About 2% of his viewers are women
Women's programs then and now use tiny dumbbells that are too light to build anything, on the false belief that lifting like a man makes you look like one
Thirty years later women are still told to use light weights to tone muscles
Women's fitness information gets softened into nonsense while also inheriting all the bro-science men get
Rather than light flyes for 'shaping', do an actual press for real muscle fiber damage
Pullovers make little sense for most women because a barrel chest is not a desired feminine trait
Partial crunches lifting the shoulders two or three inches have too little range of motion; women think they cannot get abs because they train them badly
Men are no better: compound lifts alone will not give you a six-pack
Most women who want to slim down simply have to diet; the tape reinforces diet culture
Fitness culture demonizes fat; women who want to shape their bodies should aim to add muscle and some fat through intelligent bulks
Even naturally skinny women need to gain weight to reach a respectable physique
Gimmicky programs are sold on how well they sell, not how well they work, by people who did not build their own physique that way
Cute tiny dumbbells and Barbie aesthetics are used to lure women intimidated by lifting into buying products
The tape's program of 1-2 sets of 10-15 flyes and pullovers at about 40% intensity and 2 sets of 20 crunches is garbage
Evolving sets and reps can still produce terrible programs if you do not know how to use the method
Having women simply train like men denies biological differences and individual goals; female fitness needs its own revamp
He plans to create training programs for female viewers
exercises: too light to be effective; use a real press instead
barrel-chest goal makes little sense for women
